question.title: Network Diagnostics Basics: ping, traceroute, curl -v, and dig
question.scenario: A microservice reports that it cannot connect to an external payment API at `https://api.stripe.com`. A junior engineer tries running `ping api.stripe.com` and reports: 'Stripe is completely down because ping is not responding!'
question.question: Why is `ping` an unreliable test for web API health? How do `dig`, `traceroute`, and `curl -v` methodically isolate whether a network failure is DNS, routing, firewall, or HTTP layer?
hints: Ping uses ICMP echo requests; many enterprise firewalls, CDNs, and cloud providers block ICMP packets by default while HTTP/HTTPS (ports 80/443) works perfectly.
`curl -v` prints DNS lookup, TCP 3-way handshake, TLS negotiation, and HTTP response headers.
question.answer:
1. Why `ping` is Misleading:
`ping` uses ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol). Cloud providers (AWS, Cloudflare) and security firewalls routinely drop ICMP echo requests to prevent DDoS attacks and network mapping, even when HTTPS web traffic is 100% operational.

2. Layer-by-Layer Diagnostic Workflow:
- Step 1: DNS Resolution (`dig` / `nslookup`):
  `dig api.stripe.com +short`
  Verifies whether local DNS servers resolve the hostname to an IP address. If this fails, the issue is DNS.
- Step 2: Route & Hop Tracing (`traceroute` / `mtr`):
  `traceroute -T -p 443 api.stripe.com`
  Uses TCP SYN packets on port 443 to identify which intermediate router or firewall is dropping packets.
- Step 3: End-to-End Handshake & TLS (`curl -v`):
  `curl -iv https://api.stripe.com/health`
  `-v` (verbose) outputs:
  - Resolving IP address
  - Connected to IP port 443 (verifies TCP 3-way handshake)
  - SSL/TLS handshake (verifies certificate validity, cipher suites, expiration)
  - HTTP request and response headers (verifies HTTP status codes 200 vs 403 vs 500).
question.pitfalls: Assuming a service is offline because ICMP ping times out; skipping verbose `curl -v` and guessing whether failures are DNS, TLS, or HTTP related.
question.key_takeaway: Never rely on ICMP ping to diagnose web services. Use `dig` for DNS, `traceroute -T -p 443` for routing, and `curl -v` to inspect TCP, TLS, and HTTP responses.
